summary: Union County, IL 80-ft steel fire tower in Shawnee NF, probably built c.1938-1940; 1974 bid notice required removal; now listed as gone, site undescribed.

facts.design: 80-foot steel fire tower with a cab large enough for overnight stays
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts index lists the tower as gone; no source gives the year it came down

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note places a fire tower 20 feet from a new survey mark at the site
Bob Frakes groups Atwood with towers built in 1940; conflicts with the 1938 survey note
Forest Service bid notice: tower to be sold and removed within 180 days; removal date not given

evidence.supports: location: Union County, Shawnee National Forest, Jonesboro Ranger District
evidence.quote: Union County - Shawnee National Forest - Jonesboro Ranger District
Anyone want to buy an 80-foot steel fire tower?

evidence.supports: a fire tower stood 20 feet from the new survey mark
evidence.quote: 20 FEET SOUTH OF A FIRE TOWER, AND FLUSH WITH THE GROUND.

evidence.supports: Frakes groups Atwood with towers built in 1940; cab large enough for overnight stay
evidence.quote: The 1940 Massac and Atwood towers were built with a cab large enough so someone could stay overnight.

evidence.supports: March 1974 notice; bids to be opened at the Jonesboro ranger station
evidence.quote: will open bids Friday at the ranger station in Jonesboro

evidence.supports: tower had to be removed from the forest within 180 days
evidence.quote: The only catch is that the tower must be removed from the forest within 180 days.

evidence.supports: officials said aerial fire surveillance made the tower obsolete
evidence.quote: Forest Service officials said increased aerial fire surveillance has made the tower obsolete.

evidence.supports: Frakes: almost all Illinois towers taken down or sold in early 1970s
evidence.quote: before almost all were taken down or sold in the early 1970s

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts index lists Atwood Hill as gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Frakes places Atwood among 1940 towers; a 1938 Coast and Geodetic Survey note already mentions a fire tower at the site. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone is confirmed. The 1974 Southern Illinoisan notice is quoted through the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not read. No source gives staffing, fires, removal date or the site's condition today. Brief elevation (843 ft per Wikidata) is not used.
